items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Duke was here at the time. So they brought 5 or 6 musicians; you know, Ben Webster and then came with Blanton, and Sonny Greer and Rex Stewart Stuart; they came in during the night, and I invited everybody from the clubs... we would close it, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah, Strayhorn was here, and the reason he was making arrangments for us was because Duke Ellington was in town with the show, "Jump for Joy" -- the "Jump for Joy" was downtown at the Mann Theatre. Was that in '41?

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: But that Ellighew, I don't remember hearing that.

ctx.x: Yeah, there were some Irving Brothers, but ... yeah, they were early, though. Yeah, they were. It seems like one played guitar and another one played bad piano. I think ... I don't know. But yeah, I remember the names -- but I think this was a little bit before I got out there.
And then the next name it lists is Ellighew. Duke Ellighue. Was there such a band in Los Angeles?

Duke Ellighue? No. It could have been, but see, to me, it would have made more sense now that you said that, I just thought of ... see, when like before I got here, you know, we got here in 1929 and I don't remember any of those bands. It could have been during that time that I was in school, like from '29 to '33 that I may have lost contact with those people.
